chunks: Someone congratulated another person in the presence of Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, on the birth of a son
saying to him: Congratulations for getting a rider of horses. Then Amīr al-mu’minin said:

key_terms.لِيَهْنِئْكَ: congratulations to you / may it be a blessing to you

ai.seo_question: What did Amīr al-mu’minīn say when someone congratulated another on the birth of a son with the phrase 'Congratulations for getting a rider of horses'?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the Shia emphasis on gratitude (shukr) as the proper response to divine blessings, where the congratulator’s phrase 'Li-yahni'ka al-faris' (may the rider be blessed to you) is interpreted not merely as a wish for military prowess but as a recognition of the child as a source of strength and dignity for the family. Sharif al-Radi includes this in the chapter on congratulating births to underscore that such occasions are opportunities to acknowledge Allah’s favor, aligning with the Prophetic tradition of expressing joy through thankfulness rather than mere celebration.
